name: Activity center
reason: It keeps a sitting baby in one spot with toys in reach, and unlike a walker it has no wheels.
desc: A round seat on a stationary frame that spins and bounces, with a tray of toys.

sources.name: AAP: Baby walkers, a dangerous choice

name: Baby bathtub
reason: It makes the first wobbly baths less awkward. A sink works too.
desc: A small plastic tub, often with a sloped insert that holds a newborn.
more: Until the umbilical cord stump falls off, usually within one to two weeks, a sponge bath with a warm washcloth is all your baby needs. After that, about three baths a week is plenty, since more can dry out their skin. Keep one hand on your baby the whole time, and never step away mid-bath.

name: Baby carrier or wrap
reason: Being hands-free is a real relief, but fit is personal, so try one on before buying.
desc: Fabric that holds your baby against your chest. Wraps are a long piece of cloth you tie; structured carriers buckle.
more: Parents use one for walks, chores, or settling a baby who only wants to be held. Wraps tend to suit the newborn months; buckled carriers are quicker to put on and often last into toddlerhood. Whichever you use, you should always be able to see your baby's face, with their chin up off their chest.

name: Baby food maker
reason: A blender or fork mashes soft foods just as well.
desc: A countertop machine that steams and purees fruit and vegetables into baby food.

name: Baby gates
reason: Once your baby crawls, stairs are the biggest fall risk in most homes.
span: From about 6 months, once your baby crawls
desc: Gates that block stairs or doorways, either pressure-mounted or screwed into the wall.
more: The usual spots are the top and the bottom of the stairs, plus any room you'd rather keep closed off, like the kitchen. At the top of the stairs, use a gate that screws into the wall, not one held by pressure. Pressure gates are fine between rooms, and easy to move when you need to.

name: Baby monitor
reason: Useful once your baby sleeps out of earshot. If they're in your room, you're the monitor.
desc: A camera or microphone in the nursery that sends sound or video to a parent unit or your phone.
more: Video lets you check on your baby without opening the door. Wherever the camera goes, keep it and its cord at least three feet from any part of the crib. If yours connects to Wi-Fi, change the default password when you set it up.

sources.name: CPSC: Monitor cords and cribs, 2011 recall

name: Baby neck float
reason: Neck floats can deflate quickly, and about two inches of warm water in a basin does the job.
desc: An inflatable ring that fits around a baby's neck so they float in a tub or pool.
safety: The AAP warns that neck floats can deflate quickly, and says never to use them without close adult supervision.

name: Baby powder
reason: The AAP says not to use baby or talcum powder, because breathing it in can damage a baby's lungs.
desc: A fine white powder in a shaker bottle, sold for dusting a baby's skin at diaper changes.
safety: The AAP says not to use baby or talcum powder on your baby, because breathing it in can harm a baby's lungs.

name: Baby shoes
reason: Babies who can't walk don't need shoes. Socks keep feet warm.
desc: Small soft or hard-soled shoes sized for infants.
more: Before your baby walks, their feet develop best bare or in socks. Once they walk outside, a first pair should be comfortable, with a non-skid sole and a little room to grow. Feet grow fast at this age, so check the fit about once a month.

name: Baby swing
reason: Many newborns settle in gentle motion, but a bouncer does the same job in less space. Not for sleep.
desc: A powered seat on a frame that sways your baby back and forth, with a reclined seat and a harness.

name: Baby towels and washcloths
reason: Small soft cloths are easier to handle on a wet baby, but towels you already own do the same job.
desc: Small, soft cotton cloths for washing your baby, and a towel with a built-in hood that covers the head after a bath.

name: Baby toys
reason: Toys arrive from every direction, so buy none until you see what your baby reaches for.
desc: Rattles, soft toys and simple wooden toys sized for a baby's hands.

name: Baby walker
reason: The AAP has called for a ban on walkers with wheels, and they don't help your baby learn to walk.
desc: A seat with a tray in a wheeled frame that lets a baby who can't walk yet scoot around the floor with their feet.
safety: The AAP has called for a ban on baby walkers with wheels because of injuries, especially falls down stairs.

sources.name: AAP: Baby walkers, a dangerous choice

name: Baby wash and lotion
reason: You'll use very little, and the AAP advises mild soap used sparingly and a fragrance-free moisturizer.
desc: A gentle liquid wash for body and hair and a plain lotion for dry skin, usually in pump bottles.

name: Bassinet
reason: A crib or play yard in your room does the same job.
desc: A small bed on legs that fits next to yours for the first few months.
more: The AAP recommends sharing a room with your baby for at least the first six months. A bassinet is meant for babies up to about five months, or until they can push up on their hands and knees, whichever comes first. Plan for the next bed to go in your room too. Check the label for its weight limit.

name: Bath thermometer
reason: The AAP says your wrist or elbow tells you the water is warm, not hot.
desc: A floating toy or tab that shows the water temperature in the tub.

name: Bath toys
reason: Cups and cloths from your kitchen are plenty of entertainment in the tub.
desc: Floating and squirting toys made for the bath.

name: Bibs
reason: Burp cloths cover most newborn mess, and bibs matter more once your baby drools and starts eating solids.
desc: A small piece of fabric or silicone that fastens around the neck to catch drool and spit-up. Cotton ones snap or stick closed at the back, and silicone ones have a pocket along the bottom edge.

name: Blackout curtains
reason: A darker room helps some babies nap longer, and any thick curtain works.
desc: Heavy, lined curtains that block daylight from a bedroom window.

name: Board books
reason: Thick cardboard pages survive chewing, and any picture book works for reading aloud.
desc: Small picture books with thick cardboard pages and rounded corners.

name: Short-sleeve bodysuits
reason: The base layer that goes under everything.
desc: A one-piece top that snaps between the legs, so it stays tucked.
more: Short-sleeved ones go under everything; long-sleeved ones work on their own in cooler weather. After a messy diaper, the shoulder flaps let you pull the bodysuit off downward, over the legs instead of the head. Sizes are labeled by age, but the weight range on the tag is the better guide.

name: Bottle brush
reason: It reaches the bottom of a bottle, and the CDC advises a brush used only for baby feeding items.
desc: A long-handled brush with a thick bristled head that scrubs the inside of a bottle. Smaller brushes clean nipples and valves.

name: Bottle drying rack
reason: The CDC says air-drying on a clean towel is probably more hygienic than using a rack.
desc: A small stand with pegs or prongs that holds washed bottles upside down while they dry.

name: Bottle sterilizer
reason: Boiling water or a dishwasher's hot cycle does the same job.
desc: A countertop or microwave device that steams bottles and pump parts clean.
more: Wash bottles and nipples after every feed. For most babies, hot soapy water or a dishwasher with hot water and a heated-dry cycle is enough. The CDC suggests sanitizing at least once a day for babies under two months, born early, or with a weakened immune system. Boiling them for five minutes does it.

name: Bottle warmer
reason: A bowl of warm water does the same thing, and many babies take milk at room temperature.
desc: A small electric device that heats a bottle of milk.
more: However you warm milk, test a few drops on the inside of your wrist first: it should feel warm, not hot. Skip the microwave, which heats unevenly and can leave hot spots. Once breast milk has been warmed, use it within two hours.

name: Bottles
reason: You'll need them for formula or pumped milk, and even nursing parents use a few so someone else can feed.
desc: Plastic or glass bottles with a soft nipple. Newborns use the slowest-flow nipple.
more: Start with two or three of one kind before buying a full set, since some babies are picky about nipple shape. Wash bottles and nipples after every feed, by hand in hot soapy water or in a dishwasher.

name: Bouncer or rocker
reason: A safe spot to set your baby down awake for a few minutes. Not for sleep.
desc: A low, reclined seat on a springy frame that bounces or rocks as your baby moves.
more: Always buckle the harness, and set it on the floor, never on a table, counter, bed, or sofa. If your baby falls asleep in it, move them to their crib or bassinet, flat on their back. Stop using it once your baby can sit up on their own or reaches the weight limit on the label.

name: Breast pump
reason: Most US health plans cover one, so check before buying.
desc: A hand or electric pump that draws breast milk into a bottle.
more: A double electric pump is quicker if you'll pump often, say after going back to work. A hand pump is fine for the occasional bottle. The part that touches the breast, the flange or shield, comes in sizes. The nipple should sit centered in it without pinching. Pumping shouldn't hurt; if it does, a lactation consultant can help.

sources.name: FDA: Breast pump injury and infection

name: Burp cloths
reason: You'll go through several a day. Plain cloth diapers or muslins count.
desc: Absorbent cloths you put over your shoulder when burping your baby.
more: Plain cotton cloth diapers, the flat or folded kind, are cheap, absorbent, and work as well as anything sold for burping. Keep one wherever you feed: by the bed, on the couch, in the bag. They also make a quick clean layer under your baby's head on someone else's sofa or shoulder.

name: Cabinet locks
reason: The AAP advises latches on cabinets that hold cleaning products and other hazards.
desc: Plastic latches that fix inside a cabinet door and lock when it closes.

name: Car seat add-ons
reason: The AAP says to use only inserts that came with your seat or were made by its manufacturer for that model.
desc: Padded head supports, strap covers and bunting-style liners sold separately from the car seat by another company, usually to make it softer or warmer.
safety: Use only inserts and covers that came with your car seat or were made by its manufacturer for that model, as the AAP advises.

sources.name: AAP: Car seats, information for families

name: Car seat mirror
reason: It didn't come with your seat, and you shouldn't be watching the back seat while driving.
desc: A mirror that straps to the back-seat headrest so you can see a rear-facing baby from the driver's seat.
more: Not seeing your baby's face takes getting used to, but a rear-facing seat is the safest way for a young baby to ride. If you need to check on them, pull over somewhere safe. On longer drives, an adult in the back seat can keep an eye on things.

name: Car seat stroller frame
reason: Handy for the first months, but it's outgrown when the infant car seat is.
desc: A lightweight wheeled frame with no seat of its own. Your infant car seat clicks straight into it.
more: It suits short errands: your baby goes from car to stroller and back without leaving the seat. Not every car seat fits every frame, so check that yours does. Car seats are made for travel, not sleep. If your baby falls asleep in one, move them to a firm, flat surface on their back as soon as you can.

name: Car seat
reason: Every US state requires one, and many hospitals check before you drive home.
desc: A padded seat with a harness that faces the back of the car. Infant versions have a carry handle and click into a base that stays in the car.
more: Install the base a few weeks before your due date, and have a certified car seat technician check it. Fire stations, hospitals and community programs often do this for free. Keep your baby rear-facing up to the seat's rear-facing height or weight limit. In cold weather, buckle them in thin layers, then lay a blanket or coat over the straps.

sources.name: NHTSA: Car seats and booster seats

name: Changing pad
reason: A towel on the floor works in a pinch.
desc: A contoured, wipeable pad you put on a dresser or the floor for diaper changes.
more: Set out everything you need before you start, so you never have to step away. Keep one hand on your baby the whole time, even if the pad has a strap. A towel on top saves washing the cover after every change.

name: Changing table
reason: A changing pad on a dresser does the same job, and you keep the dresser.
desc: A waist-high table with a rail and shelves, used only for diaper changes.
more: Many changes happen wherever you are: on a bed, the couch, or a towel on the floor. Whatever surface you use, keep a hand on your baby. If you change on a dresser, anchor it to the wall.

name: Coat or snowsuit
reason: For longer walks in the cold. It comes off before you buckle your baby in.
desc: A warm outer layer, or an all-in-one snowsuit, for outings in the cold.
safety: Bulky coats and snowsuits shouldn't be worn under car seat straps. Buckle your baby in thin layers, then lay the coat or a blanket over the straps.

sources.name: AAP: Winter car seat safety tips

name: Convertible car seat
reason: Your baby outgrows the infant seat, and a convertible seat is the next one.
desc: A larger car seat that starts rear-facing and later turns to face forward, used until your child outgrows it.

name: Crib bedding set
reason: Loose blankets, pillows and quilts don't belong in a crib, and a sleep sack keeps your baby warm instead.
desc: A matching bundle of quilt, pillow, crib skirt and sheet sold as one set to decorate a crib.

name: Crib bumpers
reason: Padded bumpers have been banned for sale in the US since 2022. A bare crib is the safe setup.
desc: Padded strips tied around the inside of a crib's slats.
safety: Don't use bumpers, even ones you already have. Take them out of the crib.
more: A crib with just a fitted sheet can look bare, but that's how a safe crib looks. The AAP advises against anything that attaches to the crib's slats or sides. Mesh liners attach that way too, even though the ban doesn't cover them.

sources.name: CPSC: Safe Sleep for Babies Act

name: Crib mattress
reason: Firm, flat, and snug to the crib frame. That's where safe-sleep guidance starts.
desc: A thin, firm mattress sized to fit a standard crib with no gap at the edges.
more: To check the fit, push the mattress to one side. If more than two fingers fit in the gap, it's too small for the crib. Firm means it doesn't dip when your baby lies on it. Put only a fitted sheet on top, with no toppers or extra padding.

name: Crib mobile
reason: The AAP says to take it down once your baby is on hands and knees or five months old, which leaves a short window of use.
desc: A frame that clamps to the crib rail or hangs overhead and turns soft shapes above the baby.

name: Crib
reason: It's where your baby will sleep for the next two to three years.
desc: A small bed with slatted sides. Most have a mattress height you lower as your baby learns to stand.
more: If your crib is secondhand, check that it was made after June 2011. That's when the current federal safety standard took effect, and drop-side cribs don't meet it. Check that no slats are loose, cracked, or missing, and that a soda can doesn't fit between them. Many convert into a toddler bed later, so one lasts longer.

name: Diaper bag
reason: Any backpack you already own does the same job.
desc: A bag with lots of pockets for diapers, wipes, and a change of clothes.
more: What goes in it matters more than the bag. Pack a few diapers, wipes, a fold-up changing mat, a spare outfit for your baby, and a spare shirt for you. Restock it when you get home so it's ready next time. A small pouch with the basics is easy to move between bags, cars, and parents.

name: Diaper caddy
reason: A basket or shelf you already own holds diapers and wipes just as well.
desc: A portable bin with dividers for diapers, wipes and cream.

name: Diaper rash cream
reason: A thick layer of zinc oxide paste or plain petroleum jelly protects red skin, and the ingredients matter more than the label.
desc: A thick white paste or clear ointment you spread over your baby's diaper area to keep urine and stool off the skin. It comes in a tube or tub.

name: Diaper pail
reason: It contains the smell better. A lidded trash can you empty daily works fine.
desc: A lidded bin that seals used diapers away.
more: Keep it next to where you change, and wipe it out once a week. Once your baby starts solids, tipping solid poop into the toilet first makes a big difference to the smell. Some pails only take their own refill bags, which adds a running cost; one that takes regular trash bags is cheaper over time.

name: Diapers
reason: Expect eight to twelve a day early on. Don't stockpile the newborn size, because babies outgrow it fast.
desc: Disposable or cloth diapers, sized by your baby's weight.
more: Red marks on the thighs or leaks up the back usually mean it's time for the next size. Until the umbilical cord stump falls off, fold the front of the diaper down below it so the stump stays dry. Plenty of families use a mix of disposable and cloth.

name: Digital thermometer
reason: It's the first thing your pediatrician will ask about when your baby seems unwell.
desc: A small electronic thermometer that reads temperature in seconds.
more: If your baby is three months or younger and has a temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, call your pediatrician right away. A rectal reading is the most accurate for babies, and ear thermometers aren't reliable for young ones. Label one thermometer for rectal use only, so it never ends up in anyone's mouth.

sources.name: AAP: How to take a child's temperature

name: Dishwasher basket
reason: The CDC says a mesh laundry bag you own does the same job as a closed-top basket.
desc: A small closed-top basket that holds nipples and bottle parts on a dishwasher rack.

name: Dresser
reason: It stores your baby's clothes and holds a changing pad on top, and any dresser you already own works.
desc: A low chest of drawers for folded clothes and diapers, flat and sturdy enough on top for a changing pad.

name: First feeding set
reason: A couple of soft spoons and a small bowl are all solids need at first.
desc: Small soft-tipped spoons, a shallow bowl, and a cup sized for a baby's hands.

name: First-aid kit
reason: Having the basics in one place saves a search when you need them. The kit you keep for the rest of the family covers most of it.
desc: A box or pouch of basic supplies such as bandages and tweezers.

name: Fitted crib sheets
reason: Two or three are enough. You'll change them more often than you expect.
desc: Sheets with elastic all the way around, sized for a crib mattress.
more: Use only fitted sheets made specifically for cribs. A good one stays put when you tug at a corner. For middle-of-the-night changes, keep a clean sheet folded by the crib so neither of you is searching in the dark.

name: Formula prep machine
reason: An expensive shortcut for a two-minute task. A kettle and a scoop work.
desc: A countertop machine that mixes formula powder and warm water at the push of a button.
more: Measure the water exactly as the formula label says; too much or too little affects your baby's nutrition. Use a prepared bottle within two hours, or refrigerate it. Once your baby starts drinking from it, finish within an hour and throw out what's left. For night feeds, premeasured powder in a small container leaves only the water to add.

name: Furniture anchors
reason: Cheap straps that keep dressers and shelves from tipping. Install them once and forget them.
span: Before your baby pulls up, about 6 months
desc: Straps or brackets that fix tall furniture to the wall.
more: Anchor anything tall or top-heavy: dressers, bookshelves, and the TV. New dressers come with an anti-tip kit, so install it right away. Keep toys and remotes off the top of furniture, so there's nothing your child wants to climb for.

name: Glider or nursing chair
reason: You'll spend hours sitting through feeds, and any comfortable chair with arms works.
desc: A padded chair that rocks or glides smoothly, often with a matching footstool.
more: Whatever chair you feed in, your arms should rest on the armrests without hunching while you hold your baby. Your feet should reach the floor too. Wipeable or washable fabric helps, because spit-up happens. Many end up as the bedtime-story chair long after the feeding months.

name: Going-home outfit
reason: Any sleeper works for the trip home, and it is easier to put on a newborn than a special outfit.
desc: A special first outfit, often a matching set with a hat, bought for leaving the hospital.

name: Grooming kit
reason: A kit bundles small tools you won't all use, and nail clippers are the one you need, so buy them on their own.
desc: A small case holding clippers, a brush, a comb and sometimes a nasal aspirator.

name: Hats for outdoors
reason: For outdoors: a warm hat in the cold, a brimmed one in the sun. Indoors, your baby doesn't need one.
desc: A soft warm hat for cold days, or a brimmed sun hat.
safety: The AAP says not to put a hat on your baby indoors once you're home from the hospital.

sources.name: AAP: How to keep your sleeping baby safe

name: High chair
reason: For meals once your baby starts solids, at about 6 months.
desc: A tall chair with a tray and a harness for meals.
more: Look for a wide, stable base, a harness with a strap between the legs, and a tray that's easy to take off and wash. Always buckle the harness; the tray isn't meant to hold your baby in. A chair that pulls right up to the table lets your baby eat with the rest of you.

name: Humidifier
reason: A cool-mist model can ease a stuffy nose, and it needs fresh water every day and regular cleaning.
desc: A small tank that puts a fine cool mist into the air of a room. It sits on a table or shelf out of your baby's reach.

sources.name: AAP: Stuffy nose and safe sleep

name: Inclined sleeper
reason: Banned for sale in the US since 2022. Babies should sleep flat.
desc: A sleeper that holds a baby at an angle instead of flat.
safety: Don't use one for sleep, even one you already have. Inclined sleepers have been linked to infant deaths and were recalled.
more: Babies with reflux should sleep flat on their backs too. If you have one, don't sell it or pass it on: federal law bans selling inclined sleepers, whenever they were made.

sources.name: CPSC: Safe Sleep for Babies Act

name: Infant lounger
reason: Loungers aren't safe for sleep, and a flat play mat does the same job while your baby is awake.
desc: A soft, padded pod or pillow with raised sides that a baby lies in, sold for lounging.
safety: Loungers, nests and pods are not safe for sleep. The CPSC has told parents to stop using some loungers because of suffocation risk.

name: Baby laundry detergent
reason: The AAP notes that many parents wash baby clothes in their regular detergent without problems.
desc: A liquid or powder detergent marketed for baby clothes, usually fragrance-free.

name: Long-sleeve bodysuits
reason: The warmer everyday layer, and what the AAP suggests for keeping skin covered outdoors.
desc: A bodysuit with long sleeves that snaps between the legs. Worn alone or under pants.

name: Waterproof mattress pad
reason: A washable waterproof cover protects the mattress from leaks.
desc: A washable waterproof cover for a crib mattress.

name: Mesh crib liner
reason: The AAP says these liners aren't necessary, and a bare crib is the safe setup.
desc: A thin mesh panel that ties around the inside of the crib slats, sold as a breathable bumper.

sources.name: CPSC: Safe Sleep for Babies Act guidance

name: Breast milk storage bags
reason: Flat, labeled bags store pumped milk in less freezer space than bottles.
desc: Thin, resealable plastic bags that hold a few ounces of pumped milk and lie flat in the freezer.

name: Nail clippers or file
reason: Newborn nails are sharp and grow fast.
desc: Small clippers or an emery file sized for tiny nails.
more: Trim after a bath or while your baby sleeps, when nails are soft and hands are still. Press the fingertip pad away from the nail before you clip, and file off any sharp edges. Many parents file instead of clipping for the first weeks, then switch to clippers as nails get thicker.

name: Nasal aspirator
reason: A few drops of plain saline and gentle suction clear a stuffy nose, which makes feeding easier.
desc: A soft rubber bulb, or a hand-held suction tool with a small tip, that gently pulls mucus out of your baby's nostril. Some models run on batteries.

sources.name: AAP: Stuffy nose and safe sleep

name: Night light
reason: A dim, warm light lets you find your way and change a diaper at night without switching on the overhead.
desc: A small plug-in or battery lamp that gives off a low glow.

name: Nursery decor
reason: Art and wallpaper make a room feel finished, but your baby doesn't need them for sleep or care.
desc: Wall art, wallpaper, rugs and shelves chosen to decorate a nursery.

name: Nursery storage
reason: Boxes, baskets and a laundry hamper you already own do the same job.
desc: Fabric bins, hampers and small hangers sold for a nursery.

name: Nursing cover
reason: A light blanket or muslin cloth you already own does the same job.
desc: A fabric panel with a neck strap that drapes over you and your baby during a feed.

name: Nursing pillow
reason: It takes strain off your arms and back during feeds. A regular pillow works for many parents.
desc: A firm, C-shaped pillow that wraps around your waist to raise your baby during feeds.
more: It works just as well for bottle-feeding, so either of you can use it. Use it only for feeding, while you're awake. If your baby falls asleep on it, or you start to feel drowsy, move your baby to their own sleep space. A removable, washable cover is worth having.

name: Rompers and outfit sets
reason: A bodysuit plus pants covers the same days, with fewer snaps and buttons to fight at changes.
desc: One-piece rompers, overalls and matching top-and-bottom sets sold as outfits.

name: Outlet covers
reason: The AAP advises safety plugs in all unused outlets, and you fit them once.
desc: Small plastic plugs that press into unused wall outlets.

name: Pacifiers
reason: The AAP advises offering one at naps and bedtime, because it lowers the risk of SIDS. If your baby won't take one, that's fine.
desc: A soft nipple on a shield, for sucking between feeds.
more: If you're breastfeeding, wait to offer one until feeding is going well, usually around three to four weeks. The AAP suggests offering one at naps and bedtime; if it falls out once your baby is asleep, you don't need to put it back. Don't attach one to a string around the neck, or to clothing during sleep.

name: Pants or leggings
reason: Sleepers cover the legs most days, so a few soft pairs to go with bodysuits are enough.
desc: Soft pull-on pants with a stretchy waist, worn over a bodysuit.

name: Play mat
reason: A clean blanket on the floor does the same job, but a mat gives your baby something to look at and reach for.
desc: A padded mat for the floor, often with an arch overhead that holds soft toys your baby can look at and bat.

name: Play yard (travel crib)
reason: Useful for travel or a second floor, not needed if you have a crib.
desc: A foldable crib with mesh sides that packs into a bag.
more: Practice setting it up and folding it at home before a trip; every model has its own trick. Use only the mattress it came with, and don't add a second mattress or padding on top. Many have a raised bassinet level for the newborn months, which saves bending over.

name: Receiving blanket
reason: Handy as a clean surface, a nursing cover or a light layer in the stroller, but it never goes in the crib.
desc: A thin cotton or muslin blanket, about a metre square, that hospitals often wrap newborns in.
safety: Loose blankets don't belong in your baby's sleep space. For sleep, the AAP advises sleep clothing or a wearable blanket instead.

sources.name: AAP: How to keep your sleeping baby safe

name: Scratch mittens
reason: Short nails prevent scratches better, and many sleepers have fold-over cuffs.
desc: Thin mittens that cover a newborn's hands to stop face scratches.

name: Shopping cart cover
reason: Wiping the cart handle takes seconds, and you only need it once your baby sits up.
desc: A padded fabric cover that fits over a shopping cart's seat and handle.

name: Shorts
reason: A short-sleeved bodysuit is already a summer outfit.
desc: Short pants for warm weather.

name: Sleep positioner or wedge
reason: The FDA and AAP advise against them. Flat and bare is the safe setup.
desc: Foam wedges or bolsters meant to hold a sleeping baby in one position.
safety: Don't use one, even one you already have. Lay your baby on their back on a firm, flat mattress with nothing else in the crib.
more: Positioners are sometimes sold for reflux or a flat spot on the head, but neither is a reason to use one. What helps with a flat spot is supervised tummy time while your baby is awake, and changing which way their head faces in the crib.

sources.name: CPSC and FDA: Sleep positioner warning, 2010
AAP: Flat spots and tummy time

name: Sleep sack
reason: The simplest safe way to add warmth at night once swaddling stops. Loose blankets don't belong in the crib.
desc: A wearable blanket with arm holes that zips over pajamas.
more: Choose the size by your baby's weight, using the chart on the label. They come thicker and thinner for cool and warm rooms. As a guide, your baby should wear at most one layer more than you'd need to be comfortable. Once your baby is out of a swaddle, an arms-out sleep sack is the usual next step.

name: Smart sock or vitals monitor
reason: The AAP doesn't recommend them for preventing SIDS, and false alarms add worry rather than remove it.
desc: A sock or clip that tracks your baby's heart rate and oxygen and alerts your phone.
more: If what you want is peace of mind, the steps with the strongest evidence cost nothing. Put your baby to sleep on their back, on a firm, flat surface with only a fitted sheet, in your room. If you use a monitor anyway, treat it as an extra, never as a replacement for those steps.

name: Smoke and CO alarms
reason: CPSC advises smoke alarms on every level and in each bedroom, and CO alarms on every level and outside sleeping areas.
desc: Ceiling or wall devices that sound a loud alarm when they sense smoke or carbon monoxide.

name: Socks
reason: Footed sleepers keep feet warm most of the time. A few pairs cover the days your baby wears pants.
desc: Small socks or soft booties to keep feet warm.

sources.name: AAP: Winter car seat safety tips

name: Stroller accessories
reason: Your stroller's own canopy and a blanket from home handle most weather.
desc: Add-on fans, footmuffs, organizers and weather covers sold separately for a stroller.

name: Stroller
reason: You'll use it most days for the first few years.
desc: A wheeled seat you push. Many fold down for the trunk, and some recline flat for newborns.
more: Before buying, try folding it with one hand and lifting it into your trunk, since you'll do both often. Bigger wheels handle curbs and rough sidewalks; smaller ones are lighter and fold smaller. Set the brake every time you stop, even on flat ground.

name: Swaddle
reason: Many newborns settle better wrapped. You'll stop once your baby starts trying to roll.
desc: A blanket or zip-up wrap that holds a newborn's arms snugly at their sides.
more: Wrap the arms snugly but leave the hips loose, so your baby's legs can bend up and out. Legs wrapped straight and tight can harm the hips. A swaddled baby always sleeps on their back. Zip-up swaddles are easier than folding a blanket in the middle of the night, whoever is on night duty.

name: Sweater or fleece
reason: A thin warm layer you can add or remove fast, and the kind that's safe under car seat straps.
desc: A light cardigan or thin fleece jacket to layer over a bodysuit.

sources.name: AAP: Winter car seat safety tips

name: Swimwear and swim diapers
reason: Public pools usually ask for a swim diaper, and a long-sleeved suit covers more skin in the sun.
desc: A small swimsuit or rash guard, and reusable or disposable swim diapers that hold solids in the water.

name: Teether
reason: A firm rubber ring gives sore gums something safe to chew on.
desc: A small ring or shape of firm rubber that a baby can hold and chew.

name: Teething gel
reason: The FDA says benzocaine gels can be dangerous, and that gels and teething tablets offer little to no benefit.
desc: A numbing gel or dissolving tablet put on or in a baby's mouth, sold to ease teething pain.
safety: The FDA warns that numbing gels with benzocaine can be dangerous for babies.

name: Teething necklace
reason: The FDA warns against teething jewelry after reports of strangulation and choking.
desc: A necklace, bracelet or anklet of beads, often amber, sold to soothe sore gums.
safety: The FDA warns against teething necklaces and bracelets because of the risk of strangulation and choking.

name: Two-piece pajamas
reason: Once your baby is moving a lot, a snug top and bottom are easier to change than a zip-up sleeper.
desc: A snug-fitting cotton top and pants made for sleep, sold in matching sets.
safety: In the US, sleepwear above 9 months must be snug-fitting or flame-resistant, so choose snug pajamas.

name: Weighted sleep sack or blanket
reason: The AAP says not to use weighted blankets, sleepers or swaddles on or near your baby.
desc: A sleep sack, swaddle or blanket with weighted pads or beads sewn in, sold to help babies settle.
safety: The AAP says not to use weighted blankets, sleepers, swaddles or other weighted objects on or near your baby.

sources.name: AAP: How to keep your sleeping baby safe

name: White noise machine
reason: It helps some babies sleep through household noise. A free phone app is a fine test first.
desc: A small speaker that plays steady background sound.
more: Put it well away from the crib, never on or in it, and keep the volume low. You don't need lullabies or extra features. Some families keep using one for years and bring it along for naps away from home.

sources.name: Pediatrics study: Infant sleep machine noise, 2014

name: Wipe warmer
reason: Nice idea, but most parents stop using it within a few weeks. It's not a safety or comfort issue either way.
desc: A plug-in box that keeps a pack of wipes warm.
more: If cold wipes bother your baby, holding one in your closed hand for a few seconds takes the chill off. In the first weeks, some parents use cotton pads and warm water instead. Either way, your baby gets used to whatever your routine is.

name: Wipes
reason: You'll use them for far more than diapers.
desc: Soft, damp cloths in a resealable pack.
more: Keep a pack wherever you change diapers, plus one in the car and one in your bag. Close the lid after each use, or the top ones dry out. Before buying in bulk, try one pack and see how your baby's skin does with it.

name: Zip-up sleepers
reason: You'll appreciate a zipper at 3 a.m. Snaps are slower.
desc: Footed one-piece pajamas that zip from neck to ankle.
more: Two-way zippers open from the bottom, so you can change a diaper without uncovering your baby's chest. Built-in feet mean no socks to go missing. Check the fit at the feet: once toes press against the end, it's time for the next size.
